title: Bill’s Shrimp Cocktail

items.raw: 2 pounds large shrimp (16–20 count), shell on

steps.text: Put 3 quarts of water in a large pot with the lemon halves, onion, bay leaves, peppercorns, Old Bay, salt, and parsley stems. Bring to a rolling boil and let it go 5 minutes so the water actually tastes like something.

Add all the shrimp at once, stir, cover the pot, and pull it off the burner. Let stand 3 to 5 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and just opaque at the thickest part. This is the trick — boiled shrimp turn rubbery, poached shrimp stay tender.
Drain and dump the shrimp straight into a bowl of ice water. Leave them 5 minutes to stop cooking, then drain well and pat dry.
Peel, leaving the tail on for a handle, and devein with the tip of a paring knife. Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour — cold is half the point of shrimp cocktail.
Stir the ketchup, horseradish, lemon juice, Worcestershire, Tabasco, and celery salt together. Taste and add horseradish until it clears your sinuses. Chill.
Hang the shrimp around the rim of a bowl of sauce, or pile them over crushed ice with the sauce in the center. Lemon wedges alongside.

notes.label: Buy shell-on
notes.text: the shells season the shrimp from the outside in as they poach. Peeled shrimp come out noticeably blander.

notes.label: Frozen is fine
notes.text: most “fresh” shrimp were frozen anyway. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, not in warm water.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: shrimp and sauce both keep a full day covered in the refrigerator. Do not assemble over ice until serving.

notes.label: Horseradish
notes.text: the jarred kind loses its punch within a month of opening. Buy a fresh jar for this.

openQuestion: Tell me about Bill and when this appears — Christmas Eve, birthdays, summer? I have also guessed at his cocktail sauce; if he had a specific ratio or a secret ingredient, I will put it in.
